'''Kalpina''' (劫賓那) was one of the disciples of {{ill|The Buddha|en|The Buddha|qid=Q9441|lt=Shakyamuni Tathāgata}}. He is often honorifically called '''Maha Kalpina''' and is also known as '''Konpira''' ({{ill|Konpira|ja|金毘羅}}).

Among the disciples of Shakyamuni Tathāgata, he is renowned as the '''Foremost in Knowledge of the Constellations.'''

Several accounts exist regarding his background:

# He was the son of a {{ill|Kshatriya|als|Kshatriya|am|ክሻትሪያ|ami|Satili|ar|كشاتريا|as|ক্ষত্ৰিয়|bcl|Kshatriya|be|Кшатрыі|bew|Satria|bn|ক্ষত্রিয়|br|Kshatriya|ca|Kxatriyes|cs|Kšatrija|de|Kshatriya|eo|Kŝatrijo|es|Kshatriya|fa|کشاتریا|fi|Kshatriyat|fr|Kshatriya|gu|ક્ષત્રિય|he|קשטרייה|hi|क्षत्रिय|id|Kesatria (kasta)|it|Kṣatriya|ja|クシャトリヤ|jv|Ksatriya|kn|ಕ್ಷತ್ರಿಯ|ko|크샤트리야|lt|Kšatrijai|ml|ക്ഷത്രിയൻ|mr|क्षत्रिय|ms|Kshatriya|ne|क्षत्रिय|new|क्षत्रीय|nl|Kshatriya|no|Kshatriya|or|କ୍ଷତ୍ରିୟ|pi|क्षत्रीय|pl|Kszatrija|pnb|چھتری (ذات)|pt|Xátria|ro|Casta Kșatrya|ru|Кшатрии|sa|क्षत्रियः|sd|ڪشتري|si|ක්‍ෂත්‍රිය|simple|Kshatriya|sk|Kšatrija|sq|Kshatriya|su|Satria|sv|Kshatriya|ta|சத்திரியர்|te|క్షత్రియులు|th|กษัตริย์ (วรรณะ)|tt|Кшатрия|uk|Кшатрії|ur|کھشتری (ذات)|vi|Kshatriya|zh|刹帝利|zh_yue|剎帝利|qid=Q242360}} (royal family) in a border region called Kukuta and ascended to the throne after his father. He sought knowledge by sending envoys to all four directions. Learning from merchants about Shakyamuni Tathāgata Buddha residing in the {{ill|Jetavana|de|Jetavana|eo|Ĝetavano|id|Jetavana|it|Jetavana|ja|祇園精舎|ko|기원정사|my|ဇေတဝန်ကျောင်းတော်|no|Jetavana|ru|Джетавана|sq|Xhetavana|ta|ஜேதவனம்|th|วัดเชตวัน|vi|Tinh xá Kỳ Viên|zh|祇园精舍|zh_classical|祇園|qid=Q305242|lt=Jetavana monastery}}, he traveled east to seek teachings. Along the way, he encountered heavy rain by the Chandanbhaga River and stayed in a potter's hut. Shakyamuni Tathāgata, aware of his arrival, disguised himself as an elderly monk and joined him, eventually leading Kalpina to become his disciple. ({{ill|Theragatha|ja|長老の偈}}, verses 547–556)

ruling over 36,000 subordinate states. When he sent a message to {{ill|King Pasenadi|ja|波斯匿王|qid=Q3055324}} of Kosala demanding surrender, Shakyamuni Tathāgata, in the guise of a {{ill|Chakravarti (Sanskrit term)|en|Chakravarti (Sanskrit term)|qid=Q1059400|lt=Chakravarti (ideal king)}}, revealed the limits of his power. Kalpina realized his own shortcomings and became a devoted disciple, renouncing his throne to join the Buddhist monastic community. (References: {{ill|Sutra of the Wise and the Fool|en|Sutra of the Wise and the Fool|qid=Q7650110|lt=The Sutra of Wise and Foolish}}, Volume 7, Chapter 36, and {{ill|The Hundred Stories Sutra|ja|撰集百縁経|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579608}}, Volume 9, Chapter 88)

== Past Life ==
According to the {{ill|Dhammapada|ja|ダンマパダ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 法句経|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q748878}} (Verses of the Law), in a past life, Kalpina prayed before the Buddha Padumuttara and aspired to his position as Foremost in Knowledge of the Constellations. As a guild leader of weavers, he offered alms to 1,000 {{ill|Pratyekabuddha|ja|縁覚|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2000996}} monks, thus earning merit that led to his rebirth in the heavens. Later, he offered further support to the Buddhist monastic community during the age of {{ill|Kassapa Buddha|ja|迦葉仏}}, which paved the way for his present life as the king of Kukutabhani City. His queen, named Anoja (from the people of {{lang|sa|Saagala}}), also followed the path of Buddhism and eventually ordained as a nun.

== Career ==
After Shakyamuni Tathāgata visited his hometown of {{ill|Kapilavastu (ancient city)|en|Kapilavastu (ancient city)|qid=Q30610827|lt=Kapilavastu}} and resumed his wandering teachings, Kalpina joined the monastic order along with prominent disciples such as {{ill|Aniruddha (Buddhist)|en|Aniruddha (Buddhist)|qid=Q3306373|lt=Anuruddha}}, {{ill|Upāli|en|Upāli|qid=Q984630|lt=Upāli}}, and Nandika (難提迦). Shakyamuni Tathāgata guided him with teachings, leading Kalpina to achieve enlightenment. Renowned for his deep meditative practices and solitary focus, he was described as having lived a privileged life where food was so abundant it was believed to "arise from the storehouse."
